learning_outcomes.text: Recognize the fundamental concepts of urban sociology.
Acquire knowledge about sociological theories and models related to urban space and urban change, as well as the identity and function of the planner.
Develop the ability and perspective to identify underlying problems in urban phenomena.
Learn to understand urban problems by relating them to the economic, social, and political intellectual climate.
Learn that planning is a process interacting with all social spheres, beyond merely spatial arrangement.

Relationship between Urban Sociology Theories and Planning Approaches: Planners; Utopias
Theoretical framework for current issues: Classical and contemporary theories explaining current phenomena such as filtering, gentrification, differentiation, segregation, othering
CONTEMPORARY THEORIES: Different Explanations and Models for Urban Dynamics. Chicago School; Critical Approach.

THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK FOR CURRENT ISSUES: Discussion of current phenomena such as transformation, filtering, gentrification, differentiation, segregation, othering within the framework of classical and contemporary theories.
